plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A herbaceous perennial producing large, fragrant, bowl-shaped to fully double blooms atop sturdy stems with glossy, deeply lobed foliage. It is a beloved cottage garden staple and a classic cut flower.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to China, Mongolia, and Siberia; widely cultivated in temperate gardens across North America, Europe, and Asia
plants.funFact: Peony plants can live for over 100 years, and ants are often seen on the buds feeding on nectar, though they are not required for blooming.

plants.name: Rosa gallica
plants.description: One of the oldest cultivated roses, forming a compact, suckering shrub with fragrant, semi-double to double flowers and golden stamens. It is the ancestor of many old garden roses.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June)
plants.location: Native to southern and central Europe and western Asia; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Dried petals of Rosa gallica 'Officinalis' retain their fragrance for years, which is why it was long used in medicine and perfumery as the Apothecary's Rose.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A fast-growing tropical to subtropical tree with fern-like leaves that erupts in clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers, carpeting the ground beneath when they fall.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere subtropics (May to June); October to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Pretoria (South Africa), California, Mexico, Florida, and the Mediterranean
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, nicknamed the Jacaranda City, there are tens of thousands of jacaranda trees lining the streets.

plants.name: Banksia serrata
plants.description: A gnarled, hardy Australian tree or shrub with serrated leathery leaves and tall, cylindrical flower spikes made of thousands of tiny flowers, which attract nectar-feeding birds and mammals. In the Southern Hemisphere it blooms in autumn and winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer through winter, with peak flowering in autumn (March to June in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Eastern Australia, from Queensland to Victoria and Tasmania, mostly in sandy coastal heath and woodland
plants.funFact: Banksia seed cones, called follicles, often stay sealed until fire passes, which triggers them to open and release seeds onto the nutrient-rich ash.
